sentences.text: The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 832021 at about 7.30 p.m. when Valkanayaka @ Valyanayak was going as a pillion rider on TVS XL bearing reg.No.KA16L9407 on MadadakereGadiyappana Gatti village, to attend the nature call, he stopped his vehicle, while urination on extreme side of the road, at that time, driver of Tractor bearing reg.No.KA16TC 2654 and tailor bearing No.KA16TC2655 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed from behind, due to which Valkanayka @ Valyanayak sustained fatal injuries and immediately he was taken to Government hospital at Hosadurga for treatment, wherein doctor advised him to MC Gann Teaching district hospital at Shimoga where he died in the hospital.
It is further stated that Post mortem was conducted at hospital and confirmed that the death caused due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

It is stated that prior to the accident, Valkanayka @
Valyanayak was aged about 55 years, hale and healthy and earning Rs.45,000/ per month by working as a fish seller and contributing his earnings for maintenance of the family.
Due to sudden and unnatural death of Valkanayka @ Valyanayak, petitioners lost love and affection and facing severe financial problems.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.20 lakhs from the respondents.

sentences.text: Inspite of due service of notice of the petition upon them, the respondents No.1 & 2 appeared before this Tribunal.
The respondent No.1 filed written statement wherein contended that the petitioners are not legal heirs of the deceased Valkanayaka @ Valyanayak.

The driver of Tractor bearing reg.No.KA16TC2654 and tailor bearing No.KA16TC2655 was driven his vehicle in a slow and cautious by following all traffic rules and regulations, on 832021 deceased suddenly and negligently tried to cross the road and caused the accident.
It is further contended that Tractor bearing reg.No.KA16TC2654 and tailor bearing No.KA16TC2655 was having insurance policy which is in force as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, abnormal and imaginary.
Hence respondent No.1 prays to dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The respondent No.2 insurance company filed written statement wherein contended that accident was not caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

As per section 134(c) of MV Act it is mandatory duty of the insured respondent No.1 to furnish the particulars of policy,
date, time and place of accident and name of the driver and particulars of DL.
But the respondent No.1 has not complied with statutory demand.

It is further contended that as per section 158 (6) of MV act it is mandatory duty of the concerned police station to forward all the relevant documents to the concerned insurer within 30 days from the date of information, but the Hosadurga police station has failed to forward the documents and not complied with statutory demand.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective DL at the time of accident.
The driver of the offending vehicle driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of tractor and trailer.

The rider of moped in which deceased traveling as pillion without having proper lookout vehicular movements of the road and without noticing on coming vehicles rode the moped in rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.

Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
5.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove

that the deceased Valkanayka S/o Ramasinganayka sustained grievous injury in an accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA16TC 2655 on 832021 at about 7.30 p.m. in between Mdadakere, Gadiyappana Hatti village, Hosadurga Taluk, Chitradurga577527 he succumbed to the said injury?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal representatives of the deceased ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom ?
4. What order or award ?
6. The Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and one eye witness got examined as PW2 and Ex's.
P1 to 17
were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondents have not lead either oral or Malleshnaika vs Thimmappa on 16 January, 2024

3 documentary evidence.
7. Arguments were addressed on both sides.
8. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 :

Though respondent No.1 and 2 has denied the occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and negligence of the driver of the tractor and denied that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased, but respondent No.1 has not cross examined the PW1 and denied the evidence of PW1.

Further even though counsel for respondent No.2 has cross examined the PW1 and 2 but has not at all denied that the petitioners are not the legal representatives of the deceased.
Respondent No.2 has contested only with regard to the negligence of the deceased.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is only with respect to actionable negligence.

The petitioners plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA16 TC2655 Whereas the respondent No.2 contending that Tractor and Trailor is not at all involved in the accident and deceased himself due to his negligence sustained injuries due to his self fall and to obtained the compensation has made false claim on the driver of the tractor.

But the respondent No.1 who is the RC owner of the vehicle has stated in his objection para 9 clearly stated that when the deceased suddenly and negligently crossing the road, the accident has been caused and this fact clearly shows the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.

10. Apart from this, PW2 the eye witness has also clearly stated that on that day the TVS XL was stopped on the left side of the road and the rider of the bike and the deceased pillion rider were urinating on the road side, at that time, Tractor bearing reg.No.KA16TC 2654 and trailor bearing reg.No.KA16TC 2655 came with high speed and rash and negligent manner and hit to the deceased Valkanayka to his hind portion.
Even in the crossexamination PW2 has outrightly denied the suggestion of the respondent No.2 that he has not present at the time of accident.

No where respondent No.2 has denied the involvement of the tractor and trailor in the accident and also rash and negligent of the driver of the tractor and trailor in the crossexamination of the PW2 at least by way of putting any single suggestion.
Apart from this, one Rudresh has lodged the complaint against the driver of the Tractor bearing reg.No.KA16TC 2654 and trailor bearing reg.No.KA16TC 2655 soon after the accident.

11. It can be seen from the complaint of Rudresh that when deceased Valkanayka and Tippeswamy have stopped their TVS XL at the side of the road and were urinating at that time, driver of the Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16 TC2654 and KA16TC2655 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the Valkanayka to his hind portion and thereby caused the accident.

The Hosadurga police after due investigation filed chargesheet against driver of Tractor and Trailor Malleshnaika vs Thimmappa on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56763393/
4 bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA16TC2655 for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 304A of IPC R/w 187of IMV Act.

Apart from this, on perusal of the sketch ExP6 and spot mahazar ExP4 it clearly shows that the accident had been taken place on the extreme left edge of the road which clearly shows that the deceased and the Tippeswamy were in the mud road by the left side of the tar road.
Moreover respondent No.2 has not at all challenged all the police documents.
Further it also shows that there was sufficient space on the road and even there is no suggestion about the heavy traffic on the road.

Apart from this, respondent No.2 has not examined the driver of the Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA16TC2655 who has to state about the actual facts and circumstances which caused the accident.
During cross examination, PW.1 was suggested that the accident took place due to negligence of the deceased, which was outrightly denied.

Apart from this, PW1 in his crossexamination clearly stated that the accident has been taken place on the mud road and this fact has not been denied by the respondent No.2.
12.
Apart from this, on perusal of IMV report marked at ExP7, it reveals that accident has not caused due to the any mechanical defect of the above said vehicles.

Even respondent No.1 and 2 counsel have failed to examine the driver of the Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA16TC2655 who has to give the reasons or who has to explain the situations which caused the accident.

13. Moreover the respondent No.1 and 2 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of offending Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA16TC2655, who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non examination of driver of offending vehicle is fatal to the defence of Respondent No.1 and 2.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA16TC2655 has to be disbelieved.

14. The evidence and material on record, clearly shows that accident has been caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA 16TC2654 and KA 16TC2655.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of the Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA 16TC2655.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUES NO.2 & 3 :
The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chiefexamination and deposed that he is the son, petitioner No.2 is the son, petitioner No.3(a) is the daughter in law of the deceased.
At the time of the accident and at the time of filing of the petitioner, as petitioner No.3 was alive and was entitle to the compensation.
As during the pendency of the petition, petitioner No.3 died and petitioner No.3(a) being his wife certainly entitle to the compensation.
Moreover, this fact is not disputed by the respondent.

The documents which are exhibited at Ex's.P11 to 15 i.e.,
adhaar card and ration card reflect the aforesaid relationship of the claimants with the deceased.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents, as is evident from the tenor of crossexamination of PW.1.

The counsel for the respondent No.1 argued that the petitioners being the major sons are not dependent on the deceased and relied on the rulings reported in MFA No.7070/2014(MV) wherein para No.12 it is observed Malleshnaika vs Thimmappa on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56763393/
5

that the claimant No.1 (a) to (c) were all married daughters ad claimant No.1 (d) and (e) were major son and daughter and tribunal under the circumstances was justified in holding that they were not dependent on the income of the deceased.
16. On the other hand, counsel for the petitioners relied on the rulings 2018 SC 1004 SCNew India Assurance Vs Jain.

entities.text: 2018 SC 1004 SCNew India Assurance Vs Jain
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. In this regard, in the present case, admittedly petitioner No.1 to 3 are the only three sons and they are the legal representatives of the deceased.

Though respondent No.2 has contended that petitioners are not dependent on the deceased, but in the crossexamination PW1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that they are not dependent on the income of their father.
On the other hand, PW1 has clearly stated that he is illiterate and working as coolie and his brother was studied only 7th standard.
Under such circumstances it is clear that petitioners are certainly dependent on the income of their father.

In this regard, this court fortified by the way of the decision reported in National Insurance company Vs Birendra wherein the Hon'ble Apex court has discussed in detail regarding the word legal representatives of the deceased and held that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation irrespective of the fact whether legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.
Hence, the said contention of insurance company cannot be accepted in view of Birender's case.
18. The Apex court in the said judgment further held even married sons are also entitled for compensation.

This court also cannot make any discrimination whether they are married sons or married daughters and hence, very contention that married daughters of deceased are not entitled for compensation cannot be accepted and the court has to take note of the rationale behind in coming to the conclusion of even married sons and major sons are eligible to claim compensation and hence the married daughters also entitle for compensation on all the heads and not to limit only for conventional heads.

19. Having considered the principles laid down in the judgments referred to supra, this court has taken note of recent judgment of the Apex court in Birender, wherein it is held that even married sons are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads but also on loss of dependency.
Hence, the very contention of the appellantinsurance company cannot be accepted.

20. This court also would like to rely upon the judgment of the Division Bench of this court in MFA No.118/2018 dated 2632021, wherein also this court by relying upon the judgment in Birender,
held that even married sons are also entitled for compensation not only on conventional head but also on loss of dependency.
21.

Be that as it may, since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and are entitled for compensation not only on conventional head but also on loss of dependency.

sentences.text: LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:
In the ration card (Ex.P.15) the date of birth of deceased is shown as 77 years as on1552021, which indicates that he was aged 77 years on the date of accident.
Admittedly the deceased was married and at the time of accident he was 77 years of age.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '5'.
23.

According to PW.1, at the time of accident, deceased was earning Rs.45,000/p.m. by working as a fish seller business and agricultural coolie and was hale and healthy and contributing all his earnings to the maintenance of their family.
The petitioners have not produced any documents regarding avocation and income of deceased.
In the absence of proof, this Tribunal has to consider the income notionally for calculating the compensation.

As the accident took place in the year 2021 and since the deceased was a semi skilled worker, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.15,000/ p.m. Needless to mention, also taking into consideration the age of the deceased,
nature of his work as well as the present cost of living.
24.

In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

entities.text: 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Sarala Verma's case towards his future prospectus if 10% of the salary is added it would be around Rs.16,500/ (15,000 + 1500).
The deceased was married and having three dependents.
Hence 1/3rd of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/3 of Rs.16,500/ works out to Rs.5,500/.
Income for consideration is Rs.11,000/ (16,500 - 5,500).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,32,000/ (11,000 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '5'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.6,60,000/ (1,32,000 X 5).
25. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/ (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of loss of spousal consortium, parental consortium and loss of love & affection.

sentences.text: 26. LOSS OF ESTATE:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
27. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.

28. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : 6,60,00000 2 Loss of Consortium : 1,45,20000 3 Loss of Estate : 18,15000 4 Funeral Expenses : 18,15000 Total Rs.8,41,500=00

Hence,
petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.8,41,500=00.

sentences.text: REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
30. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Though the insurance company contended that the owner of Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA 16TC2655 has violated the terms & conditions of the policy, no evidence is adduced to prove such breach of terms & conditions of the policy by the respondent No.2.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the insurer and respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending Tractor bearing reg.No.KA16TC2654 and Trailer bearing No.KA 16TC2655 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
31. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the findings given on issues No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
: ORDER :
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,41,500=00 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit together with interest, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for the compensation amount in equal proportion.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioner No.1 to 3 through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw an award accordingly.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
30. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
Though the insurance company contended that the owner of Tractor and Trailor bearing No.KA16TC2654 and KA 16TC2655 has violated the terms & conditions of the policy, no evidence is adduced to prove such breach of terms & conditions of the policy by the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the insurer and respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending Tractor bearing reg.No.KA16TC2654 and Trailer bearing No.KA 16TC2655 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
